reference.title: Early preliminary results on co-seismic deformation of the island of Samos associated with co-seismic slip following the October 2020 Mw 6.9 Samos earthquake (Greece)

inversion.method: Published Irmak (2020) source model adopted in Toker et al. (2021), Figure 2b, for coseismic Coulomb stress calculations; GCMT-based source and waveform-fit depiction. The present JSON is a categorical figure digitization, NOT a new InSAR inversion or source inversion.
inversion.green_function_model: Not specified for the reproduced Irmak (2020) model in the supplied Toker et al. (2021) paper.
inversion.notes: NOT AN INDEPENDENT TOKER ET AL. FINITE-FAULT INVERSION. Figure 2b in Toker, Senturk & Bayik (2021) reproduces/adopts an Irmak (2020) GCMT-based/waveform-constrained Samos slip illustration for Coulomb stress analysis. The paper describes the source for its stress calculations as a "uniform-slip" model despite visually heterogeneous colours in the figure. This JSON captures only the PLOTTED SLIP FIELD, rather than independent slip coefficients or a claim about the inversion parameterization. ORIGINAL SUBFAULT GRID IS NOT DOCUMENTED IN THE PAPER. We sample the published figure at an ARBITRARY 80 × 20 image-regularized raster (~1 km per display cell) spanning approximately -40 to +40 km on the plotted along-strike axis and 20 km across the displayed dip-coordinate window. These 1600 cells are NOT AUTHOR INVERSION PATCHES. The 40 × 20 km plane mentioned in the manuscript pertains to the Coulomb stress model; do not confuse it with the longer plotting window. Slip values are figure-legend CLASS MIDPOINT ESTIMATES using the displayed 0–2.7 m categorical colourbar, and are not original numerical inversion values. First white class represented by display-zero, possibly including low slip. Overlaid contours, arrows, and hypocenter marker were excluded; the latter and masked positions were imputed from neighbours and flagged in the accompanying QA CSV. No time-dependent rupture velocities or slip-vectors were reconstructed. The displayed fault panel plots signed dip-relative distances with a 0 line around the GCMT hypocenter. Patch depths in this JSON are SCHEMATIC ONLY: zero on that plot has been provisionally anchored to the GCMT 12 km focal depth, yielding a 6 km schematic top. The PDF does not georeference the original patch centers or define absolute depth at every display pixel. Per-patch latitude and longitude are therefore null. The model geometry and nominal rake -79.9 are printed directly by Figure 2b (strike 270, dip 37, rake -79.9), whereas Table 1 / stress-calculation text lists rake -95 for the GCMT-based receiver-plane calculation; preserve that discrepancy. InSAR measurements in Toker et al. (2021) were used to characterize coseismic SURFACE DEFORMATION, not to invert the original figure slip model. The paper reports UTC origin 11:51:34.8; event.origin_time uses the canonical 11:51:26 UTC entry from the existing Samos database (Aktug et al. 2021) to enable automatic multi-model matching. The Toker reported timestamp is retained in model_variant.

model_variant.source_model: Irmak (2020) source adopted/reproduced by Toker et al. (2021)
